components.name: acceptance
components.responsibility: Owns the end-to-end lanes that boot a gateway and a world in-process and play through login, walking, and trading.
components.why: Without it a protocol or session regression is only caught by a player.

components.name: admin-api
components.responsibility: Owns the operator HTTP API for kicks, bans, broadcasts, and live metrics.
components.why: Without it operators would need database access or a restart to moderate a live world.

components.name: asset-pipeline
components.responsibility: Owns the build step that packs sprites into atlases and compresses maps for shipping.
components.why: Without it the client would download thousands of loose sprites and uncompressed maps.

components.name: audio
components.responsibility: Owns Web Audio playback for ambient loops and effects keyed by simulation events.
components.why: Without it the game is silent.

components.name: client-core
components.responsibility: Owns the client game loop: reconciles server deltas into local state and turns input into intents.
components.why: Without it the client is a static picture; nothing moves and nothing is sent.

components.name: client-state
components.responsibility: Owns the client-side world model: known creatures, tiles, inventory, and the player's own view.
components.why: Without it the renderer and UI have nothing to draw.

components.name: content-items
components.responsibility: Owns every item definition: weapons, armor, consumables, and their attributes.
components.why: Without it there is nothing to equip, loot, or trade.

components.name: content-loader
components.responsibility: Owns loading and indexing content packages for servers and clients, with hot reload in dev.
components.why: Without it content is only files on disk; nothing can look an item up by id.

components.name: content-maps
components.responsibility: Owns the world map: towns, hunting grounds, and spawn tables as tile records.
components.why: Without it there is no ground to stand on.

components.name: content-monsters
components.responsibility: Owns creature definitions, loot lists, and AI behavior scripts.
components.why: Without it the world is empty of anything to fight.

components.name: content-schema
components.responsibility: Owns the JSON Schema for items, monsters, spells, and maps, with generated Rust and TypeScript bindings.
components.why: Without it content packages have no contract and neither servers nor editors can trust them.

components.name: content-validate
components.responsibility: Owns the CI check that every content package parses and every cross-reference resolves.
components.why: Without it a typo in a loot list would ship and crash a world at spawn time.

components.name: desktop-shell
components.responsibility: Owns the Electron wrapper that packages the web client with native windowing and auto-update.
components.why: Without it players who want a desktop app fall back to the browser and lose auto-update.

components.name: devtools-cli
components.responsibility: Owns the `mmo` developer CLI: start a local world, seed accounts, run migrations.
components.why: Without it a new developer needs a page of shell commands to get a world running.

components.name: editor-core
components.responsibility: Owns undo history, document model, and save/export shared by both editors.
components.why: Without it each editor would reinvent undo and the two would save incompatible files.

components.name: event-bus
components.responsibility: Owns the NATS publisher and subscriber wrappers that link world servers, login, and admin.
components.why: Without it servers cannot hand sessions to each other or receive operator commands.

components.name: gateway
components.responsibility: Owns the public socket endpoint: accepts client connections, authenticates sessions, and routes frames to the right world server.
components.why: Without it no client can reach a world; it is the single door into the game.

components.name: input
components.responsibility: Owns keyboard, mouse, and touch capture mapped to game actions.
components.why: Without it clicks and hotkeys never become game actions.

components.name: legacy-bridge
components.responsibility: Owns the compatibility shim that speaks the 8.6-era protocol to old clients and translates it to the current schema.
components.why: Without it players on the old client cannot connect; with it, two protocols must be kept in step.

components.name: login-server
components.responsibility: Owns account login, character list, and world selection before a client is handed to a gateway.
components.why: Without it players cannot authenticate or pick a character.

components.name: map-editor
components.responsibility: Owns the map editor UI: tile brushes, spawn placement, and house layout.
components.why: Without it designers would edit map JSON by hand.

components.name: net-client
components.responsibility: Owns the WebSocket transport, reconnection, and frame decoding in the browser.
components.why: Without it the client cannot talk to a gateway.

components.name: persistence
components.responsibility: Owns Postgres repositories for accounts, characters, and houses, plus the migration runner.
components.why: Without it every character resets on restart and no account exists.

components.name: protocol
components.responsibility: Owns the wire message schema: opcodes, message structs, and versioning that every server and client speaks.
components.why: Without it servers and clients have no shared language; a mismatch here breaks every connection.

components.name: protocol-codegen
components.responsibility: Owns the generator that turns the Rust schema into protocol-ts.
components.why: Without it the TypeScript codec would drift from the Rust schema on the first change.

components.name: protocol-docs
components.responsibility: Owns the hand-written protocol reference: opcode tables, the handshake sequence, and the review notes behind each version bump.
components.why: Without it the only description of the wire format is the Rust source, and client authors outside the repo have nothing to read.

components.name: protocol-ts
components.responsibility: Owns the generated TypeScript encoders and decoders that mirror the Rust message schema.
components.why: Without it the browser client cannot read a single byte the server sends.

components.name: renderer
components.responsibility: Owns the isometric scene graph: which sprites draw where, in what order, with which lighting.
components.why: Without it the world model cannot become pixels.

components.name: renderer-webgl
components.responsibility: Owns the WebGL2 backend: batching, texture atlases on the GPU, and shaders.
components.why: Without it the scene graph has no backend and the canvas stays black.

components.name: server-config
components.responsibility: Owns typed configuration loading (TOML plus environment) shared by every server binary.
components.why: Without it each binary would parse its own config and drift on defaults.

components.name: sim-bench
components.responsibility: Owns the Criterion benchmarks that guard tick throughput.
components.why: Without it a slow tick would ship unnoticed until a live world lagged.

components.name: sim-combat
components.responsibility: Owns damage formulas, conditions, and the attack resolution that runs inside the tick.
components.why: Without it creatures cannot hurt each other; combat is the loop the whole game is built around.

components.name: sim-core
components.responsibility: Owns the authoritative tick loop, world state, and the entity tables every other simulation crate mutates.
components.why: Without it no world state advances; every server tick and every replay depends on its ordering guarantees.

components.name: sim-economy
components.responsibility: Owns loot tables, vendor pricing, and the gold sinks that keep the economy in check.
components.why: Without it there is nothing to earn or spend, and gold would inflate without limit.

components.name: sim-pathing
components.responsibility: Owns A* and flow-field pathfinding over the tile map, including creature avoidance.
components.why: Without it monsters stand still and players cannot click to walk.

components.name: sim-scripting
components.responsibility: Owns the Lua scripting host that lets content scripts react to simulation events and schedule actions.
components.why: Without it every quest, spell, and NPC dialogue would need a Rust change and a redeploy.

components.name: sim-testkit
components.responsibility: Owns fixtures and scenario builders shared by every simulation crate's tests.
components.why: Without it each crate would rebuild the same worlds by hand and tests would drift apart.

components.name: sprite-atlas
components.responsibility: Owns atlas metadata and sprite lookup shared by the renderer and the editors.
components.why: Without it sprite ids cannot be turned into texture regions anywhere.

components.name: sprite-editor
components.responsibility: Owns the sprite editor UI: atlas packing preview and animation frames.
components.why: Without it artists cannot preview how sprites pack or animate in game.

components.name: ui-kit
components.responsibility: Owns the React components (windows, buttons, tooltips) styled like the classic client.
components.why: Without it every screen and editor would style its own windows and the look would fragment.

components.name: voxel-prototype
components.responsibility: Owns the voxel rendering spike that tests whether a 3D view of the tile map is feasible on the current scene graph.
components.why: It answers a design question; nothing ships from it yet, so a product import from it is a warning sign.

components.name: web-client
components.responsibility: Owns the browser game client: the React shell, canvas mount, and the routes players see.
components.why: Without it there is no game to play in a browser.

components.name: wire
components.responsibility: Owns binary framing, compression, and the XTEA-style session cipher on top of raw sockets.
components.why: Without it messages cannot be delimited or encrypted, and nothing crosses the network intact.

components.name: world-server
components.responsibility: Owns a running world: drives the simulation tick, applies player intents, and broadcasts state deltas.
components.why: Without it the simulation has no process to run in and no players to serve.

health.headline: Parts depend on each other
health.meaning: These components import each other, directly or through others, so neither can change alone.

health.headline: Parts depend on each other
health.meaning: These components import each other, directly or through others, so neither can change alone.
health.suggestion: Move the shared contract into one lower component or reverse one import.

health.headline: Parts depend on each other
health.meaning: These modules import each other, so neither can change alone.
health.suggestion: Move the shared contract into one lower component or reverse one import.

health.headline: Core rules import an I/O detail
health.meaning: A core component imports an adapter, so its rules are tied to one storage, transport, or engine.

health.headline: Core rules import an I/O detail
health.meaning: A core component imports an adapter, so its rules are tied to one storage, transport, or engine.
health.suggestion: Put a port near the core rules and make the adapter depend on it.

health.headline: Client and server are directly coupled
health.meaning: Client code imports server code (or the reverse) directly instead of a shared contract.
health.suggestion: Move the shared interface into a contract component used by both sides.

health.headline: Product code imports support code
health.meaning: Product code imports tooling, test, or experiment code, which can ship or break the build.
health.suggestion: Move the imported behavior into product code or keep it in the build path.
